entities.label: Text
entities.summary: The Epistle of James is a foundational text of Christian scripture, attributed to James, the brother of Jesus and the leader of the Jewish Christian community in Jerusalem. Written in the early 2nd century CE, the epistle is a collection of wisdom teachings, practical advice, and theological insights that offer guidance on living a virtuous life, addressing social and economic issues, and navigating the complexities of faith. Its significance extends beyond the early Christian community, as it has shaped the development of Western Christianity and influenced the broader cultural and intellectual landscape of the ancient world. The epistle's enduring relevance lies in its continued appeal to readers seeking wisdom, guidance, and spiritual growth, as well as its continued influence on Christian theology, ethics, and practice.
